status: Colour display update complete. Desktop map renders correctly, counter text contrast passes in both themes, and saved campaign is unchanged. Prior eight rules tests and active campaign simulations pass.
request: Offline browser game inspired by Tigers in the Snow on the TRS-80, with similar retro graphics and turn-based gameplay.
scope: Original implementation and scenario, not a reproduction of copyrighted code, artwork, manual, or exact map.
decisions: help.html provides a standalone offline/GitHub Pages player guide and sourced historical background. Help & History opens separately from the game; guide includes walkthrough, controls, current mechanics, Undo, saves, FAQs, history and distinctions from the original SSI game.

Undo Move button restores full pre-move snapshots in reverse order, including positions, movement points, town control, score and dispatches. History is session-only and clears on successful combat, End Turn, restart, import or reload; invalid orders do not clear history.

Movement destinations use small white dots with dark backing, not yellow fills or dashed hex outlines. Terrain colours remain unchanged; yellow outlines identify the selected formation and pink double outlines identify towns.
Primary target is a full desktop browser, not mobile. Fit the complete battlefield to desktop viewport height and keep commands beside it; narrow-screen layout is only a fallback.
Use local HTML, CSS and JavaScript; no server or remote assets required at runtime.

Use retro canvas hex graphics with ASCII counters and a compact command panel. User requested colour: green forests, blue rivers, amber ridges/roads, rose towns, red German counters, blue American counters, yellow movement/selection outlines. Keep symbols alongside colour cues.
Use ROT.js hex pathfinding for movement and supply instead of inventing a pathfinding engine.
Player commands the German offensive; American computer opponent defends and counterattacks.
Include terrain costs, zones of control, combat odds, retreat, supply, weather, reinforcements and timed victory objectives.
Save game state in browser local storage with JSON export/import fallback.
Keep this file updated with observable results and design decisions, not private reasoning.
